li.label: threw darts at a wall
li.description: Three of my darts hit the board. The rest are a problem for whoever owns that wall.

li.label: getting the hang of darts
li.description: They all land on the board now. Where on the board is still a negotiation.

li.label: threw a decent round of darts
li.description: Aimed at the twenty, hit the twenty. Twice. I am choosing to ignore where the third one went.

li.label: threw darts well
li.description: The triple twenty is a thin little box, and my hand has started to know the way there without me.

li.label: rarely misses at darts
li.description: People have started calling my shots for me before I throw. I keep making them right.

li.label: mastered darts
li.description: A board, three darts, and eight millimetres of triple twenty. I have stopped looking at the rest of it.

li.label: flailed at the bag
li.description: I hit the bag until my arms stopped listening. The bag seemed fine with it. My knuckles disagree.

li.label: finding the rhythm
li.description: Somebody told me to stop punching faster and start punching on time. Annoyingly, it works.

li.label: worked the bag properly
li.description: Swing, swing, hit. The bag comes back and my fist is already there waiting for it.

li.label: worked the bag well
li.description: I stopped counting the beat out loud. My shoulders count it now.

li.label: rarely drops the rhythm
li.description: People train next to me to borrow my tempo. I pretend not to notice.

li.label: mastered the bag
li.description: The bag swings, I answer. It has stopped being exercise and started being a conversation I always win.
